chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Salih ibn Khalid and Ubays ibn Hashim, from Thabit ibn Sharih, from Ziyad ibn Abi Ghiyath, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who had a debt of a known amount in dirhams. When the due date arrived, he did not have dirhams, nor did he have anything except dinars. So he said to his creditor, 'Take from me dinars at the exchange rate of the day.' He (the Imam) said, 'There is no harm in that.'

key_terms.بِصَرْفِ الْيَوْمِ: At the exchange rate of the day
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay a debt in a different currency than specified if the original currency is unavailable?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permits a debtor to settle a dirham debt using dinars by applying the spot exchange rate (*sarf al-yawm*), thereby avoiding the prohibition of *riba* (usury) inherent in fixed-rate currency swaps. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness and the prevention of exploitation in financial transactions, distinguishing between permissible debt settlement and prohibited currency trading.
